# Archived Assessment Handbook 2026

Fictional evaluation document. Scope: assessment administration for the 2026 policy year. Effective dates are supplied separately in the corpus manifest. This document must be read alongside other selected sources when the question names another office or location.

## Submission deadline

The 2026 assessment portfolio deadline is 20 September at 17:00 local studio time.

Assessment administration is separate from routine lesson attendance. A portfolio submission is not the same event as an in-person examination. Staff preserve the assessment year and the timestamp of each received item instead of substituting a later acknowledgement. For this section the desk records the request under ASSESSMENT-2026-01. The reference groups correspondence; it does not change the deadline or amount stated above. A correction must preserve the original entry and record the reason for the change.

## Working example: submission deadline

Consider a case where a student prepares a portfolio while waiting for examiner feedback. The immediate question concerns submission deadline, not every rule in the assessment file. The administrator checks assessment dates, rubric versions, and appeal correspondence before replying. A common error is that a student uses an archived video limit for the current assessment year. Read the named source and policy year before treating a nearby number as the answer. Record which document supported the explanation so that another staff member can reproduce the check. If the request also mentions a different service, preserve it as a separate issue instead of assuming that one approval covers both activities.

## Cross-service boundary

This assessment document does not grant authority over unrelated activities. A staff member should distinguish the stated rule from a future booking, payment, or discretionary approval. A family may ask several questions in one message; answerable portions should cite the relevant source while missing facts remain unresolved. An unanswered detail must not be inferred from an adjacent fee, deadline, room number, or event identifier. In particular, general guidance about assessment dates, rubric versions, and appeal correspondence is not a substitute for an explicit rule about a different programme.

## Handling incomplete requests

When a assessment request omits the student, location, policy year, or relevant date, the desk records the missing information and asks for it. The original wording is preserved in the working notes. Staff avoid copying identity documents into teaching chat or broad distribution lists. A later clarification supplements rather than overwrites the request. This distinction matters when a student prepares a portfolio while waiting for examiner feedback. A response acknowledging receipt is administrative correspondence and should not be represented as approval of an exception.

## Audit example and non-equivalence

The reviewer reconstructs the event from assessment dates, rubric versions, and appeal correspondence. For example, an entered reference code may identify correspondence without proving that money moved, a class place was reserved, or a consent decision changed. The reviewer compares the dated source with the actual record and records unresolved inconsistencies. Similar words across offices are not proof of identical policies: deposit, credit, submission, and acknowledgement each have a specific role in their own service. The desk retains source identity rather than combining conflicting numbers into a new undocumented rule.

## Final archive

The final 2026 assessment archive must retain the rubric version printed on the examiner’s signed sheet.

This is the last substantive instruction in this source. The closing check must be performed after the ordinary service tasks, not inferred from an earlier example. Preserve a short completion note with the responsible staff role and source reference. If the closing check cannot be verified, mark the item unresolved rather than copying a previous day’s completion status. End of policy text.
